note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919: the first county council election in the five electoral areas that replaced the county electoral divisions of 1899, 21 seats. Polled Thursday 3 June 1920 (Belfast News-Letter, 3 June 1920, p. 6, "To-day's Polling"); counted at the Courthouse, Crumlin Road, Belfast, by Alexander Millar, secretary of the county council, as returning officer. Lisburn area (three seats): 5,768 valid votes, 230 spoiled, quota 1,443; 10,697 electors. Barbour was elected on the first count with 2,796. The paper prints the defeated candidates' first preferences but not Fitzgerald's or Downing's (together 1,701). Count 2, Barbour's surplus of 1,353: Fitzgerald 857, M'Cance 295, Best 107, Sinclair 71, Downing 23. Count 3, Best's votes: Fitzgerald reached the quota with 1,526 and was elected; his small surplus was not transferred. Count 4, Sinclair's 692 votes: Downing 164, to 1,376, and was elected; M'Cance 142, to 1,002. The list of candidates on polling day prints Downing as "Patrick Downey, Montaghs". J. Stouppe F. M'Cance D.L., chairman of the old council, was defeated (and later co-opted). The minute of the council's first meeting also records the chairmen of the rural district councils, who sat ex officio, and the co-opted members; they were not elected and are not listed here.
